recentItems.description:

DJ Vlad breaks down the Dallas case that ended with Yella Beezy being found guilty of capital murder in the killing of rapper Mo3, including how a VladTV interview became part of the prosecution’s trial strategy and closing arguments. Vlad revisits the timeline: Beezy’s rise after signing with L.A. Reid’s HitCo, the Roy Lee shooting, Beezy’s 2018 ambush, Mo3’s “219,” and the alleged fallout that prosecutors tied to the murder case.

The discussion covers the “get my lick back” interview clip, Kewon White’s conviction, pending cases involving Davon Brown and Jerry Johnson, and the reported $40,000 cash withdrawal that became a key issue at trial. Vlad also compares the case to Little Durk’s legal situation, discusses defense attorneys including Drew Findling, Brian Steele, and Bryan Shook, and shares why he believes appeals could follow.

#YellaBeezy #Mo3 #VladTV #DallasRap #DJVlad

recentItems.title: Yella Beezy's VladTV Interview Used in His Trial (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, we revisit Yella Beezy's return to VladTV, where he opened up about the aftermath of being shot and explained why he chose not to speak publicly about the people he believed were responsible.

He also recalled that the late Nipsey Hussle was one of the first people to reach out and check on him following the shooting. Reflecting on his recovery, Yella Beezy discussed the realities of surviving such an experience before shifting gears to share his thoughts on what he called "angry local rappers," humorously breaking down what he viewed as the "starter kit" for becoming one.

To hear more, including Yella Beezy's comments about fellow Dallas rapper Mo3, check out the full interview above.

recentItems.title: Mo3's VladTV Tells His Life Story & Discusses Yella Beezy Beef (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In 2019, the late Mo3 told his life story from his upbringing in Dallas up through his entry into the music industry. He recounted some of the issues he had with artists in his city and the remorse he felt for his mother after his illegal activity began affecting her household. Mo3's conversation with Vlad offers a candid portrait of his life and lays out the obstacles he overcame. Following his passing in 2020, Yella Beezy was recently arrested and charged for his alleged involvement in Mo3's death.

--------
Terrance “Gangsta” Williams sits down with VladTV to break down the New Orleans politics surrounding the Cash Money and No Limit reunion run, including Lil Wayne performing with Boosie at LSU instead of joining Birdman and the crew onstage. Williams points back to Essence Festival as an early sign Wayne wasn’t fully embracing the reunion, while reflecting on Wayne’s history with Birdman and Cash Money Records.

The conversation also covers Mystikal’s legal situation, his reported 20-year sentence, and the reality of returning home later in life. Williams weighs in on Turk being left off the tour, his fallout with B.G., Juvenile, Mannie Fresh and Birdman, and why he believes Turk missed a major moment in Hot Boys history. From family loyalty to rap business, prison time and legacy, this clip offers an inside look at New Orleans hip-hop’s most complicated relationships.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/R2trf1_EZT4
--------
In this VladTV conversation, Marlow Bates and Tamir Stanfield reflect on Baltimore’s Murphy Homes housing projects, Lexington, and the street dynamics of the 1980s, explaining how different buildings and crews operated during the heroin trade. They discuss money, family ties, and why some details remain off-limits because people connected to that era are still alive.

As crack cocaine began spreading through Baltimore, Bates and Stanfield say they made a conscious decision not to get involved, choosing to stay with heroin after seeing the effects of crack and freebasing in New York. The interview also touches on missed legitimate business opportunities, including a possible stake in the Apollo Theater after Nicki Bond and plans for a McDonald’s franchise, both interrupted by prison. They also mention Busy Bee, the Bronx hip-hop scene, and Curtis Blow while connecting Baltimore’s streets to wider East Coast culture.

--------
Rene “Boxer” Enriquez sits down with VladTV to recount a violent period tied to the Mexican Mafia, drug houses, and East L.A. street politics. In this segment, Enriquez discusses David Gallegos, a made member who had reportedly fallen out of favor after an incident involving Tom Marquez in Moravia. After receiving word from Benjamin Peters that Gallegos was marked, Enriquez says the situation unexpectedly came to him at a drug house he controlled.

He details how Gallegos was given heroin in what he describes as an intentional overdose, the frantic moments that followed, and the decision to dump the body near Olympic Boulevard by the Sears Tower area. The conversation also touches on Chuck “Chuco” Castro, the 1995 RICO case, FBI informants, Sylvia Golden, and how Mexican Mafia hits were carried out for status rather than payment. A stark look inside prison gang culture, loyalty, fear, and organized crime in Los Angeles.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/h2XcCgDEtDs
--------
In this VladTV interview, Tito “TJ” Dominguez details the peak of his South Florida empire, claiming he operated with 30 airplanes, dozens of boats, multiple mansions and a fleet of Lamborghinis while making massive monthly profits as a drug smuggler. Dominguez explains how he became the world’s largest Lamborghini dealer, with territory spanning Miami, New York and Texas, and even says he tried to buy the Lamborghini factory when it entered receivership. He also discusses investments in Jefferson Bank, a major cell phone company, and other businesses.

Dominguez recalls wild moments in Fort Lauderdale, including driving a Formula One car down Sunrise Boulevard and a 200 mph Lamborghini incident on I-95 that he says landed in Newsweek. He also describes receiving keys to four cities and being invited to dinner with President Ronald Reagan after contributing heavily to the Republican Party—prompting him to question the Secret Service vetting process.
